children: An Australian man was charged with terrorism-related offences on Friday after police raided his home in Sydney.
The 35-year-old was refused bail after being charged with collecting or making a document connected with terrorism and possessing violent extremist material.

Hilda Sirec, Deputy Commissioner National Security at the Australian Federal Police, said police will allege the man possessed literature that could be used to turn a vehicle into an improvised bomb for a possible terror attack.

"At this stage, we believe he was acting alone. We have no information to suggest the alleged offender had identified targets or locations, or had obtained the capability for the vehicle-borne improvised explosive device," she told a news conference.
Two other men were also charged in connection with the investigation, one for hindering the police investigation and the other for alleged firearms offences.
The police did not name any of the men and it is not yet known if they have obtained legal representation.
Police said there is no ongoing threat to public safety.
